principles: A receipt must be auditable on its own: whoever reads it can tell what was required of the run.
Only the tool's own records are evidence; anything a caller can author is not an input to a gate decision.
Tightening a check is a different act from loosening it, and only one of them is safe to allow.
Every relaxation is bounded and visible: both pins, both receipts, a reason and the receipt ids used.
Where the proof cannot be made, refuse rather than accept a reason in its place.
drivers: B-a745 F-002 left a known-false receipt in place for the life of the story because the correction was refused as a pin change.
Immutability today conflates loosening with tightening, so the only remedies are a fixture standing in for the receipt or a waiver, both of which weaken the record.
A selector that prints on every branch is invisible in the current receipt, so nobody can audit for it after the fact.
The gate is consumed by DONE, so any change must fail closed and must not create a new path a caller can drive.

options.name: A-narrowing-only-repin-proved-from-recorded-receipts
pros: Corrects a false receipt with a proof the tool itself produced, so no new caller-authored input reaches the gate.
Keeps both pins and receipts, so the record shows what was believed before and after.
The one-narrowing-per-recorded-receipt-set bound stops a chain of re-pins from homing in on a hand-picked run.
Persisting the selector makes vacuous selectors findable in existing stories, not just future ones.
cons: outputTail is bounded, so absence can only be asserted within the retained tail and the proof must say so.
An engineered failing run remains possible: an author could drive a genuine run to fail in a way that makes the desired selector absent. This is the residual gap and must be named.

options.name: B-reason-bearing-supersede-without-proof
pros: Simple; any wrong pin can be corrected with an explanation.
cons: A reason is not evidence; this reopens evidence-shopping through the back door and is exactly what the seatbelt exists to prevent.

options.name: C-relax-immutability-outright
cons: Removes the seatbelt entirely; a pin could be moved to whatever matches, which destroys the meaning of a mechanical receipt.

rationale: Option A is the only one that lets a false receipt be corrected while keeping the property the seatbelt protects: the gate still decides from tool-recorded facts alone. Options B and C both admit caller judgement into the gate, which is the failure mode B-ec67 introduced the seatbelt to stop. The cost of A is that its proof is bounded by what the tool retained and that an engineered failing run is not excluded; both are named in the pre-mortems and the second is either bounded by the decision or recorded as an accepted limitation rather than papered over.

preMortem.scenario: Evidence-shopping by repeated narrowing: an author re-pins repeatedly, each step proved, until the selector matches only one favourable run.
preMortem.trigger: No bound on how many times a selector may be narrowed against the same recorded evidence.
preMortem.consequence: The seatbelt is defeated one legal step at a time.
preMortem.mitigation: A set of recorded receipts admits at most one narrowing; a further re-pin requires a new recorded receipt that the current selector wrongly matched, and a fixture asserts the second attempt against unchanged receipts is refused.

preMortem.scenario: A forged failing transcript is used as the narrowing proof.
preMortem.mitigation: Transcripts are not an input at all: the proof reads only receipts the tool wrote, and a fixture asserts that passing output or a transcript argument is rejected rather than considered.

preMortem.scenario: A pin whose old selector never matched a failing run is re-pinned anyway, on the strength of a reason.
preMortem.trigger: The implementation falls back to a reason when no failing receipt exists.
preMortem.consequence: The refusal path becomes optional, which is the same as not having it.
preMortem.mitigation: With no recorded failing render the re-pin is refused; a fixture covers the empty-evidence case and asserts the refusal names the missing proof.

preMortem.scenario: An engineered failing receipt: the author drives a genuine run to fail in a way that makes the desired selector absent, then uses it as the narrowing proof.
preMortem.trigger: The proof cannot tell an incidental failure from one arranged to shape the evidence.
preMortem.consequence: A narrowing is accepted that serves the author rather than the check.
preMortem.mitigation: The decision must either name a bound that closes it (for example requiring the failing receipt to predate the re-pin request and to share the story material with the compared receipts, or restricting admissible selectors to declared status discriminators) or record it as an accepted limitation in CLAUDE.md; the implementation must not claim it is mechanically excluded.

preMortem.scenario: The persisted selector is caller-injected onto a receipt that was earned under a different selector.
preMortem.trigger: The selector field is added to a caller-facing schema rather than the tool-owned receipt block.
preMortem.consequence: The audit record can be forged.
preMortem.mitigation: The field lives inside the tool-owned receipt, which every caller-facing schema strips; a fixture attempts to inject it through verification_evidence_add and asserts it is ignored.
